page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores using an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression register in the bottom 10%. However, the multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scale to average levels. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, consistently perform in the middle 50% tier, as do PassMark CPU and memory scores.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is its reliance on older Intel Broadwell architecture, which limits single-threaded execution speeds but offers stable, dedicated multi-core execution. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides a predictable resource density for workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU cores without the premium cost of newer generation architectures. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, Redis database operations, and moderate multi-threaded processing, while being less optimal for single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM inference.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data reveals a performance tradeoff: single-core CPU execution and single-threaded compression tasks perform in the lower percentiles, whereas multi-core operations, memory bandwidth, and Redis SET operations achieve average tier results. Qualitatively, the instance offers a cost-effective option for legacy multi-threaded applications. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, caching layers, and general-purpose database operations that do not require high single-threaded performance.
